info.title: Hunter API
info.description:
Find and verify professional email addresses and manage Hunter resources.
Hunter's own MCP servers forward the calling AI client's User-Agent in a reserved `X-MCP-USER-AGENT` request header. It is read only for usage attribution and to record which AI clients an account has connected from, and never changes a response. Per-request attribution resolves it to a fixed list of known clients; the first call from each new client also stores the User-Agent as sent, so a client Hunter does not yet recognise can be identified. There is nothing for an integration to send here.
Hunter's MCP servers also identify themselves with `X-SOURCE: hunter-mcp` or `X-SOURCE: hunter-chatgpt`. These reserved markers attribute server-side actions to the MCP channel, separately from ordinary API and product usage. They do not replace API authentication. Ordinary API clients do not need to send these markers.

get.description: Each campaign carries `editable`. It is true when the API key's user owns the campaign or is a team admin or owner, and only then can that user add recipients to it.
When a recipient has asked Hunter to delete their address, with a claim or a California DROP request, their `email` is null (HUN-23599).

201.description: Add campaign recipients. `data.skipped_recipients` lists the addresses that this request did not add, from both `emails` and `lead_ids`, each with its `reason`. It is `null` when no address was skipped.

Remove campaign recipients. On a draft campaign, the recipients are removed and listed in `data.recipients_removed`. On a started campaign, the recipients stay in the campaign and no more emails are sent to them: they are listed in `data.recipients_canceled`, with the count of canceled pending emails in `data.messages_canceled`. A recipient not contacted yet gets the canceled status, also when their emails are not created yet. A recipient already contacted keeps their status (sent, opened or clicked) and gets no new follow-up. `data.skipped_recipients` lists the addresses that this request did not change, each with its `reason`: `not_in_sequence`, or `no_pending_messages` when sending to the recipient already stopped (for example, they replied, or they were canceled before). It is `null` when no address was skipped.

post.description: Queues one test message per follow-up of the sequence, in step order, to the supplied address. When A/B testing is enabled on a step, both variants are sent. Subjects are prefixed with [TEST]. Returns 422 when the sequence has no step, a step is missing its subject or body, the sequence has no email account, the account cannot send, or the recipient cannot be contacted. At most 30 test emails can be queued per 10 minutes.

get.description:
Each lead carries `department` since HUN-23171. It was already a filter on this endpoint, but was never emitted, so a caller could filter on a field it could not read back.

When the person behind a lead has asked Hunter to delete their address, with a claim or a California DROP request, the lead is returned without it: `email`, `confidence_score`, `verification.date` and `verification.status` are null (HUN-23599).

A manually claimed phone number, or one covered by DROP, is returned as `phone_number: null`. The phone is also withheld when screening is unavailable; the lead and its other contact details remain.

Filter by sequence with `sequence_ids[]`. The former name `campaign_ids[]` is still accepted as an alias; when both are sent, `sequence_ids[]` is used (HUN-20893).

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Free-text search over first_name, last_name, company, website and email. Every word must match one of these fields, so a query with more words can return fewer leads. An email address returns only the lead with that exact email. Use `sort=relevance` to get the best matches first (HUN-23628).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The order of the leads. `newest` returns the most recently created leads first, `oldest` the oldest first. `relevance` returns the best matches first for a `query` or `position` search, and the newest first otherwise; leads with the same relevance come newest first. Any other value returns 400 (HUN-23628).

post.description:
A manually claimed phone number, or one covered by DROP, is returned as `phone_number: null`. The phone is also withheld when screening is unavailable; the lead and its other contact details remain.

Creates a lead, or adds an existing lead to the requested lists. When an `email` matches a lead already on your team, the request is additive: it adds only the missing list memberships and returns 201 rather than an email duplicate error. When the matched lead belongs to a teammate, the request still adds it to your lists, and the teammate's lead itself is only updated if you have permission to edit it. A request without an `email` is never matched by email — it does not reuse an existing email-less lead — though a lead with an identical name, company, and list is still rejected as a duplicate.

Accepts `department` since HUN-23171, normalized to its canonical key so a localized display label ("Sales") is stored as `sales`. Lead attributes are not modelled field-by-field in this contract yet — the response uses the generic resource envelope — so this note is where the accepted set is recorded.

When another request is creating leads for the team, returns 409 with `lead_creation_in_progress` and `Retry-After: 1`. Retry the request after one second.

409.description: Lead creation is busy for this team; retry after one second.

put.description:
A manually claimed phone number, or one covered by DROP, is returned as `phone_number: null`. The phone is also withheld when screening is unavailable; the lead and its other contact details remain.

When creating a new lead while another request is creating leads for the team, returns 409 with `lead_creation_in_progress` and `Retry-After: 1`. Retry the request after one second. Existing leads can still be updated.

put.description:
Create or update up to 100 leads in one call. Each lead is matched on `email` and written in its own transaction, so one invalid lead does not cancel the others. The team's lead limit is checked for each new lead using the current committed lead count. If an item would exceed that limit, earlier successful items remain saved and that item returns a `leads_limit_reached` error. If another request is creating leads for the team, the new lead's item returns `status: failed` with error `lead_creation_in_progress` and code 409. Retry only those failed items after one second; other items still run normally. The response is always 200: read `status` and `errors` of each result to know what happened to each lead. The call is free and consumes no request.

parameters.name: company_list_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the static company list to find lookalikes for. Provide exactly one of company_list_id or domain.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name of one company to find lookalikes for (e.g. stripe.com). A URL is accepted and cleaned to its domain. Provide exactly one of company_list_id or domain. An unknown domain returns an empty list.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Bias the ranking toward a given country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. us). This is a ranking signal, not a hard filter: companies from other countries may still appear.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Only return companies in the given size range (e.g. 51-200). To send several ranges, use Rails-style bracket encoding (size[]=51-200&size[]=11-50); a repeated plain key (size=51-200&size=11-50) keeps only the last value. Companies without a known size are excluded.

parameters.name: industry
parameters.description: Only return companies in the given industry (matched by name, case-insensitive). To send several industries, use Rails-style bracket encoding (industry[]=SaaS&industry[]=Fintech); a repeated plain key keeps only the last value. Companies without a known industry are excluded.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of lookalikes to return. Because the size and industry filters are applied after ranking, a narrow filter can return fewer.

get.summary: Find lookalike companies from a company list or a domain
get.description: Finds companies that look like the ones in one of your company lists, or like one company given by its domain. The seed companies are excluded, and we return the most similar companies ranked by a similarity score. This endpoint is not paginated: it returns a single ranked page of the top limit results, so the offset parameter is not supported and returns 400 if supplied. This call is free.

A 429 with the error id `restricted_account` means the account is blocked, suspended or delinquent; further requests with the same API key are then rejected before reaching the API for up to 10 minutes, while the account and usage endpoints stay available.

county.description: US county name, such as "Cuyahoga County". Requires country "US" and its state.

date.description: Inclusive calendar-date range in YYYY-MM-DD format. Either bound may be omitted to leave that side of the range open. Applied dates, including those resolved from a natural-language query, are returned in meta.filters.funding.date and can be reused for pagination.

discover_toggle_boolean.description: Boolean accepted by Discover job-opening toggles. Only true/false and 1/0 (case-insensitive strings). Aliases such as on/yes/y/off/no are rejected with 400, matching Api::Discover::Validations#boolean_literal?.

discover_job_openings_filter.description: Filter companies by LinkedIn job openings. Department values come from the jobs-index vocabulary (not a frozen enum). Unknown departments return 400.

hiring.description: When true, only companies currently hiring.

include_closed_roles.description: When true, include closed roles in the openings match.

discover_request.description: Use headquarters_location to include or exclude company locations. Country is required for state or city filters. States must be regions supported by Hunter's company location data. State codes are case-insensitive and surrounding whitespace is ignored. US states normalize to bare codes (CA); other regions normalize to country-prefixed ISO 3166-2 codes (FR-IDF). A bare code is accepted with its country (IDF with FR). The United Kingdom supports GB-ENG, GB-SCT, GB-WLS, and GB-NIR. Counties such as GB-WAR and GB-HRT return a validation error; use a city or choose a supported region. State is required for US cities and optional for other countries. US counties take the county name with country US and its state, such as Cuyahoga County with US and OH.

industry.description: Industry names to include or exclude.

company_type.description: Hunter company types to include or exclude.

technology.description: Technology slugs to include or exclude.

limit.description: Number of companies to return. Every plan can request up to 100 companies.

offset.description: Number of companies to skip. Only plans with Discover paging can set an offset above 0.

filters.description: Applied structured filters that can be reused for pagination. Funding date ranges resolved from natural-language queries are returned in funding.date as explicit, inclusive YYYY-MM-DD dates, preserving the date window when reused on a later day.

strict_boolean_filter.description: A boolean filter. Query-string clients may use the documented case-insensitive aliases.

source_type.description: Deprecated: use `provenance`. "found" or "generated". Its values never change, so an address with provenance "previously_found" will return "found" here.

provenance.description: Where the address came from. "found": the address was seen on a public web page. "inferred": it was worked out from the person's name and the company's email pattern. "previously_found" is coming: found on a page but not confirmed there in the last 90 days. More values may be added, so treat an unrecognized value as unknown rather than an error. Distinct from `type`, which is the role of the address.

department.description: Department value stored by Hunter's classifier, such as `finance & accounting`.

phone_number.description: Null when Hunter holds no phone number for the person, or when the number is on the California DROP list.

departments.description: Counts keyed by the department values stored by Hunter's classifier.

department.description: Counts keyed by the department values stored by Hunter's classifier. Only email addresses with a known department are counted, so the sum can be less than total.

seniority.description: Counts keyed by seniority. Only email addresses with a known seniority are counted, so the sum can be less than total.

phoneNumbers.description: Claimed numbers are omitted. Empty when phone screening is unavailable.

phone.description: Null when claimed for removal or when phone screening is unavailable.

generic_resource_response.description: Generic envelope for V2 resource operations whose detailed schema is not yet in the contract.

email.description: The address messages are sent from.

sending_status.description: `warming` while inbox protection or a progressive-sending ramp-up runs, even if the account is disconnected. Otherwise `active` when connected, and `paused` when disconnected or backing off after transient sending errors.

daily_limit.description: Maximum number of messages sent from this account per day.

sender_name.description: Display name used in the From header. May be `null` for Outlook accounts, whose sender name lives in the Microsoft profile.

default_account.description: Whether this is its owner's default sending account. Per user, so on a team several accounts can each be the default for their own owner.

signature.description: The account's signature as sanitized HTML, or `null` when none is set.

custom_tracking_domain.description: Hostname the team's tracking links, open-tracking pixels, and unsubscribe links use, for example `track.example.com`. `null` when the team has no custom tracking domain, the domain is not verified or its SSL is not ready yet, or the team's plan does not include custom tracking domains. Hunter's shared tracking domain is used in all those cases.

sending_schedule.description: The default send windows a new sequence created by the requesting user would use. A sequence can override these.

start_time.description: Start of the sending window, `HH:MM` in `time_zone`.

end_time.description: End of the sending window, `HH:MM` in `time_zone`.

time_zone.description: IANA or Rails time zone name, for example `Europe/Paris`.

enabled.description: Whether inbox protection is currently protecting the account.

status.description: `null` when inbox protection was never set up for the account.

step.description: Step to create. Optional for a new step (the next step is used). Required with `variant`, where it names the existing step that gets a Variant B.

variant.description: Set to `B` to add Variant B to an existing `step`, which turns A/B testing on for the sequence. Omitted fields are copied from the step's Variant A. A Variant B whose subject and body both match Variant A is refused.

body.description:
Plain text or HTML. Line breaks and blank lines in plain text, and `

` paragraphs in HTML, are kept. The body is stored as the editor's HTML (`

` and `
`), also when `message_format` is `text`.

message_template_id.description: ID of a message template whose subject, body, and format fill omitted fields.

email.description: The address the test messages are sent to.

company.description: Company name to resolve to a domain.

perfect_match.description: Only return an exact company-name match.

multi_domain_search_request.description: Filter set for the multi-domain search. Multi-value filters accept a comma-separated string (the v2 convention). At least one filter is required.

domain.description: Comma-separated domain names, 25 at most. A URL is cleaned to its domain. Hidden and unknown domains are dropped. With two or more remaining domains, the page spreads its rows across them (up to limit divided by the number of domains for each, never more than limit in total) and returns no next_search_after cursor.

seniority.description: Comma-separated seniority levels: junior, senior, executive.

job_title.description: Comma-separated free-text job titles. A person matches when their position matches any of the titles. Independent of department and seniority.

verification_status.description: Comma-separated verification statuses: valid, accept_all, unknown.

required_field.description: Comma-separated fields that every returned person must have (AND): full_name, position, phone_number.

exclude_already_saved.description: When true, omit people already saved as leads in your account. This refines a search but does not satisfy the at-least-one-filter requirement on its own.

limit.description: Number of rows to return per page.

search_after.description: Opaque pagination cursor from meta.next_search_after. Omit for the first page.

per_domain.description: When true, include a per-domain result breakdown in meta.

name.description: Masked display name — first name plus last initial (e.g. "Ada L."). Null when either name part is missing. The full last name is only returned by the reveal endpoint.

provenance.description: Where the address came from. "found": the address was seen on a public web page. "inferred": it was worked out from the person's name and the company's email pattern. "previously_found" is coming: found on a page but not confirmed there in the last 90 days. More values may be added, so treat an unrecognized value as unknown rather than an error. Distinct from `type`, which is the role of the address. Null when no provenance is recorded for the address.

reveal_handle.description: Opaque, signed handle identifying this row for the reveal endpoint. Never the raw email id.

next_search_after.description: Cursor for the next page, or null on the last page. Pass it back as search_after.

params.description: Echo of the applied filters. Multi-value filters are returned as arrays.

per_domain.description: Per-domain result breakdown. Present only when per_domain was requested.

lead_upsert_item.description: One lead of a bulk upsert. Same fields as the single lead upsert.

email.description: The email address that identifies the lead. Required.

leads_list_id.description: The list the lead must belong to. Cannot be combined with `leads_list_name`.

leads_list_ids.description: The lists the lead must belong to. Cannot be combined with `leads_list_name`.

leads_list_name.description: The name of a static list. The list is created when it does not exist yet. Cannot be combined with `leads_list_id` or `leads_list_ids`.

custom_attributes.description: Custom attribute values keyed by slug. Merged into the values the lead already has; a blank value clears that key.

leads.description: The leads to upsert, at most 100 per request. Each entry is matched on `email` against the leads of your team: a match is updated, anything else is created.

data.description: One result per submitted lead, in the order they were submitted.

index.description: Position of the lead in the submitted array.

lead.description: The stored lead. Null when the item failed.

csv_data.description: The CSV content. Comma and semicolon separators are both detected. The server rejects anything over 10 MB once encoded, which is a byte limit and so cannot be expressed as maxLength. Over 100,000 rows is rejected. Send a large CSV as JSON: percent encoding can treble a form-encoded body, which the proxy rejects at 25 MB before the endpoint sees it.

leads_list_id.description: Identifier of the static list the leads should land in. Must belong to your team. Omit it to pick a destination on the configuration page.

file_name.description: Name shown for this import in the imports history. A longer name is truncated rather than rejected, so no maxLength is declared.

size.description: Company size range (e.g. "51-200"). Null when unknown.

similarity_score.description: Similarity score ranking this company against the seed.

results.description: Number of lookalike companies returned after filtering.

params.description: Echo of the applied parameters. Multi-value filters are returned as arrays.

company_list_id.description: Present when the seed is a company list.

domain.description: The cleaned seed domain. Present when the seed is a domain.
